blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, trade taxes — duties, tariffs, cross-border levies — are a strategic input to sourcing decisions, not a back-office formality. Where a company sources its materials, where it builds, and which corridors it uses to move goods are all shaped by the taxes that meet the goods at every border. Although these taxes look operational, they can change the landed cost of a product by double-digit percentages, and therefore change which sourcing strategies are genuinely competitive.

The best senior leaders treat tariffs the way they treat currency exposure — a background variable that quietly shapes the margin if you leave it alone, and one that can be actively managed if you bring it into your thinking early. Provided that you model the tax landscape alongside the cost landscape, sourcing decisions become much sharper.

Whereas most companies discover trade taxes at the invoice stage, mature ones build them into the first conversation with a new supplier. The difference, across a decade, is measured in points of margin that the first group never even knew they were leaving on the table.

items.q: According to the text, how should trade taxes be understood at senior level?
options: As a back-office formality handled at invoicing
As a strategic input to sourcing decisions
As a purely legal compliance obligation
As a fixed cost that cannot be influenced
items.why: "trade taxes… are a strategic input to sourcing decisions, not a back-office formality."

items.q: By how much can trade taxes change the landed cost of a product?
options: By exactly the tariff rate quoted
items.why: "they can change the landed cost of a product by double-digit percentages."

items.q: The text compares managing tariffs to managing…
items.why: "treat tariffs the way they treat currency exposure — a background variable…"

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Where a company builds is shaped by border taxes.
Tariffs are best left to be discovered when the invoice arrives.
Mature companies raise trade taxes early with suppliers.
Modelling tax alongside cost makes sourcing decisions sharper.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro critica descobrir os tributos na fase de fatura; ele defende trazê-los para a primeira conversa.

items.q: What does the phrase "leaving on the table" suggest about the first group of companies?
options: They forgo margin they could have captured, without realising it
They deliberately sacrifice margin for speed
items.why: Inferência: "points of margin that the first group never even knew they were leaving on the table" — perdem margem sem perceber.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver mostrando ao novo diretor de sourcing o que os tributos mudaram. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Come and look at this with me for a second. This is the supplier we signed last year — the one everyone called the cheapest option. On paper, the unit price was clearly the lowest on the table.

Now watch what happens when I add the tariff line and the customs duties for that corridor. The landed cost jumps by roughly fourteen percent. And here — this nearer supplier, the one we passed over because the quote looked higher — once you include the taxes that meet the goods at the border, it actually lands cheaper.

So the point I want you to take away is this: the number on the quote is not the number that hits our margin. Whereas the old team compared invoices, I want you comparing landed costs, corridor by corridor, before you ever shortlist a supplier.

Bring the tax landscape into the first conversation, not the last. Model it alongside the cost, the way we model currency exposure. Do that consistently, and over a few years those points of margin add up to something the finance director will genuinely notice.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What was said about last year's supplier when it was signed?
options: It was the nearest supplier available
It had the highest quality rating
It was called the cheapest option, with the lowest unit price on paper
items.why: "the one everyone called the cheapest option. On paper, the unit price was clearly the lowest."

items.q: By roughly how much does the landed cost jump once tariffs and duties are added?
items.why: "The landed cost jumps by roughly fourteen percent."

items.q: What does Oliver reveal about the nearer supplier they passed over?
options: It lands cheaper once border taxes are included
It has the same landed cost as the first supplier
It was rejected for quality reasons
items.why: "once you include the taxes that meet the goods at the border, it actually lands cheaper."

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "the number on the quote is not the number that hits our margin"?
options: The quoted price omits the taxes that ultimately affect profitability
The finance director sets the quote
Margins should never be discussed with suppliers
items.why: Inferência: o preço cotado ignora tributos de fronteira, que é o que de fato afeta a margem.

items.q: What change in behaviour is Oliver asking the new director to adopt?
options: To compare landed costs early, rather than invoices after the fact
To always choose the nearest supplier
To defer all tax questions to the finance director
items.why: Inferência: "Whereas the old team compared invoices, I want you comparing landed costs… before you ever shortlist a supplier."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We treat tariffs as a strategic input, not an afterthought." A strategic input is…
options: a factor deliberately fed into a high-level decision
items.why: Strategic input = entrada estratégica: algo que você considera de propósito ao decidir.

items.q: "The landed cost came in higher than the quote once duties were added." Landed cost means…
options: the price shown on the original supplier quote
the freight charge on its own
the total cost of a product delivered to its destination, including taxes
items.why: Landed cost = custo no destino: o total já com tributos e transporte.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Tariffs are a ___ variable — they quietly shape the margin if you ignore them."
items.why: Background variable = variável de fundo: age silenciosamente sobre a margem.

items.q: "Most firms only notice the tax at the invoice stage." This means they notice it…
options: when the bill is issued, after the decision is made
items.why: Invoice stage = fase de fatura: tarde demais, quando a conta chega.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "Ignoring tariffs meant we were ___ points of margin without realising it."
items.why: To leave on the table = deixar na mesa: abrir mão de ganho que estava disponível.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de sourcing e tributos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Finance still has to sign off on the new sourcing corridor." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the landed-cost model across every buying team." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two buyers pushed back on switching suppliers." They…
options: resisted or objected to the idea
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to model tariffs early, but nobody followed through." They…
options: failed to carry the plan to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Renegotiating that one duty line really moved the needle on margin." This means it…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
